author: HypedLaunches
quoted_text:
First of all, I want to apologize for my earlier posts. Out of frustration, I used words like "scam" and "rug." Looking back, those were the wrong words to use.

Looking at all the posts from the last days, all with different perspectives, I think it's important to recognize that there are multiple different groups involved in the Kinetiq airdrop/pre-sale, each with other incentives:

• Team members – they want to build a successful protocol and token.

• Private investors – they invested early and benefit from long-term appreciation. Their allocation is only 7.5%, spread across 30+ well-known participants in the Hyperliquid ecosystem, with unlocks starting next month. They have every incentive to see the token succeed. Even with current prices, we don't have to feel sorry for them because they gonna have a very nice return on their investment.

• Token holders – they obviously want price appreciation.

• Farmers – they spent 46 weeks earning points, expecting that those points would eventually translate into an airdrop. In crypto, points almost always signal future rewards, especially when there isn't any communication suggesting otherwise. And they continued at the same pace as S1, with 800k points per week, which creates the same expectation, an airdrop. 

I think it's good when reading posts about the airdrop/pre-sale to look in what group he or she is. If we talk about myself, I was 75% in the "farmers" group and 25% in the holders group. That's ofcourse the reason I'm disappointed. 
I also saw posts from people with big followers defending this move, but their names popping up in the private seed round, so that's also explainable.  

Some latest comments about the airdrop/pre-sale:

- I don't agree with the argument that "we don't need farmers." Farmers generated a big part of the protocol activity and revenue over the past year. They played an important role in getting the protocol to where it is today.

- A pre-sale price of $0.26 doesn't feel fair when the token had pumped around 75% just a few days earlier.

- The 10-day claim window also feels unnecessarily restrictive when claiming requires a significant amount of capital. I even ended up lending some funds to friends so they could afford to claim.

Last but not least, criticism is important, and I hope the feedback from the community helps improve future launches. I still disagree with several decisions that were made, but calling it a scam or a rug was the wrong way to express that. In the end, I hope lots of teams succeed building in the hyperliquid ecosystem because otherwise only Shoku will eat.

And for myself, I move on and focus on other teams. Wish you all the best.

This is important, because it speaks directly to my vision for what the future of the StonkBrokers product line looks like.

If we break it down into simple terms: DeFi being used as the rails for everyday investment products inside banks, combined with myself as a developer of financial software, leads to a very clear future.

Banks, exchanges, financial firms and potentially even nation states using smart contracts built by myself and StonkBrokers to process, guide and give users access to peer to peer financial markets.

The goal is to cut out unnecessary middlemen and redirect more of that yield back to humans around the world.

Someone holding stock tokens could monetize those assets and generate yield through something as simple as one click staking.

Underneath that experience sits Uniswap liquidity and, oftentimes, v4 hooks that allow us to build increasingly sophisticated financial products directly around that liquidity. Maybe one day we even help create a superior v5 process.

This is exactly the game plan for our options exchange contracts: staking, leverage trading and other financial processes built around these hooks and powered by decentralized liquidity.

On the front end, this could look no different than a high APY savings or investment account offered by your bank.

On the back end, the yield and financial infrastructure could be powered by StonkBrokers smart contracts, Uniswap liquidity and the broader StonkBrokers DeFi suite on Robinhood Chain.

The user may never even need to know they are interacting with DeFi.

That is the future I am building toward: StonkBrokers becoming financial infrastructure underneath the products people already understand and use every day.

This also explains why the tweet that “hooks were a mistake” is laughable.

The mistake in logic is believing the core use case for Uniswap v4 hooks was to create the next pump and dump or meme stock coin instead of financial technological infrastructure for the global economy.

Hooks are programmable financial rails.

Options, leverage, automated liquidity strategies, yield products and eventually financial products that banks, exchanges and institutions can put directly in front of everyday users.

If your measurement of whether hooks succeeded is how many tokens pumped because of them, you’re measuring the least important part of what they enable.

The future is a user seeing a simple one click investment or high yield product on the front end, while Uniswap liquidity, hooks and smart contracts quietly power the financial infrastructure underneath it.

That is the game we are building StonkBrokers for.

text:
a16z 本周三笔新投，都围着 AI，但不在赌更大的模型。
它在铺落地：数据在哪，Agent 走哪条网，攻防怎么跟。
更关键，创始人身份成了 thesis：谁有资格讲数据主权、国家级攻防、平行网络与对抗。

1、Conway Research / Underdog
端侧个人 AI。 邮件、日历、会议、杂务，跑在用户自己的设备上。口径：数据留在本机。
创始人 Sigil Wen。多伦多出身，17 岁去 SF，睡过 WeWork，退学做 AI。20 岁拿 EB-1A，办 Extraordinary，帮高技能人才赴美——这既是移民故事，也是进入美国 builder 网络的入口。
标签：
- Thiel Fellowship：每年全球约 20–25 人，辍学两年、约 10 万美元种子加泰尔人脉，录取率不到 1%；十年间 Fellow 公司总值曾被报超 700 亿美元，校友含 Figma、Scale AI。这是筛选器，不是奖学金——Sigil 等于被泰尔网络认证过。
- Spearhead：Naval 与 Jeff Fagnan 创办，给入选创始人约 200 万美元自管基金、拿自己基金的 carry，逻辑是「把最好的创始人变成下一代 VC」。多届下来投出大量早期项目与独角兽。Sigil 成最年轻成员，重量在直接管钱的 Naval 网络，不在头衔。
- Airchat：Naval 与 Brian Norgard 做的语音优先社交产品；Naval 的产品哲学直接注入其中——他说“我们不想对内容进行审核，但会对语气进行审核”。
Thiel 给身份认证，Naval 给产品与基金入口，a16z 给第一轮下注。三股线交在一个人身上。 政治光谱清楚：移民、科技精英、下一代 builder——压成「有资格讲数据主权」的人。a16z 称领投其第一轮。

2、Armadin
面向企业与政府的自主进攻安全。 AI 攻击者集群持续打自身环境，输出可验证杀伤链，再推动修复。
创始人 Kevin Mandia。美军网络调查背景，Mandiant 创始人——从政府/军方调查传统里长出来，不是 SaaS 安全切进来。
2013 年 2 月 APT1 报告：把七年、上百受害方（多数在美）的窃密，归因到中国境内网络，并指向解放军 61398 部队；公开大量 IOC。中国外交部/国防部否认。美国国会随后引用该报告做决议。私营公司把「匿名黑客」做成「具名敌人」，attribution 从技术判断变成公共事件。Mandia 上国会作证，Fortune 封面级人物；Mandiant 成美中网络对抗里最强的私人部门符号。
资产线：FireEye 超 10 亿美元收购 Mandiant → 后拆分、改回 Mandiant → 再进 Google。卖的不只是进攻安全产品，是被连续接手的国家级安全能力。 联合创始人含 Travis Lanham 等前 Google / Mandiant 红队背景。a16z 与 Accel 共同领投 Series B。
政治光谱上，他站在对华强硬与国家安全一侧，且是操作者不是评论员：谁定义攻击者，谁更有资格卖反制。

doxx
Agentic Defined Networking。 为人及其 AI Agent 提供平行私有网络：私有浏览、P2P、设备与 Agent 组网。
创始人 Barrett Lyon。
2003 年创办行业早期 DDoS 缓解公司 Prolexic，后被 Akamai 以约 3.7 亿美元收购，技术并入其边缘安全。
New Yorker 写过他追僵尸网络；早年协助 FBI/英方追踪俄罗斯 DDoS 勒索团伙，相关人获刑。
后又创办 Defense .Net，被 F5 收购。两次创业、两次被大厂收。
平行网络表面是隐私与组网，底层是「谁能提供不被看见、又不失控的基础设施」。党派色彩弱，执法信用硬——正好撑起 a16z 对平行网络与对抗的 thesis。

三家分落消费助手、企业安全、网络基建，是同一条外溢链上的三截。
共同点：a16z 在买故事、身份、政治光谱的站位。模型外溢之后，稀缺的是谁能替某一类人讲出正当性。

text:
孔剑平博士 @JackKongNano ：投资赚钱主要靠运气！

如果你信了大佬嘴里的运气，那你可就太天真了。

表面是运气，其实全是顶级人类认知与赔率博弈。

大家都知道孔博士投资长鑫拿到了大结果，从今天的视角回看，底层逻辑非常清晰：

1. 逆向抄底
实际上他当年参与嘉楠耘智，玩的就是硬核的矿机ASIC芯片设计。他对半导体产业链、晶圆代工、硬件周期的暴涨暴跌那一套太熟悉了。2020年长鑫最惨、亏损极其严重的时候，大部分互联网VC根本不敢碰这种动辄几十上百亿资本开支的重资产无底洞，但他懂硬件周期的规律，看懂了估值不到200亿的长鑫处于极低位，这叫逆向认知。

2. 焊死下限
存储芯片是整个半导体工业的粮食，也是国产自主可控最核心的骨头，大陆几乎没有第二家能规模化做通用 DRAM 的。合肥政府被称为最强耐心资本，加上国家战略支持，长鑫这个局从一开始就注定只能成功不能失败。这就相当于跟最强的地方政府和国运绑在一起，把投资下限死死锁住了。

3. AI超级周期
这几年AI大爆发，HBM和通用DRAM直接进入超级周期，全球三大存储原厂产能供不应求，芯片价格涨上天。长鑫顺势搭上了这趟超级列车，上市后超募资金一口气又能拿出上百亿继续搞技术研发和测试基地，直接杀进全球竞争的第一梯队。

他在大家不敢下注的时候，买了一张国家战略主干道上的船票。下限靠合肥政府和国产替代兜底，上限靠AI爆发和超级周期拉满。所谓的运气，只是当他把所有的概率和赔率都算明白之后，时代正好吹过来的一阵东风罢了。

认知不够的人，风吹过来也根本抓不住。

text:
I'm amazed that people are still defending Accountable.

Dozens of millions of dollars have been lost because people trusted Accountable's NAV dashboards, which proved to be totally useless.

The clearest example of Accountable's incompetence is Neutrl's case.

Just 1 day before Neutrl suspended withdrawals, Accountable's Neutrl dashboard was still showing the protocol as overcollateralized.

Then Neutrl revealed that users were facing a ~49% loss.

Think about how insane that is.

People were relying on a "transparency dashboard" that suggested the protocol was fully backed, only to find out a few days later that nearly half of the funds were gone. 🤡

If this is not a sign of gross incompetence, I don't know what else to say. By the way, Accountable never said sorry to the users who lost money trusting it.

And I keep seeing the argument that "it's not Accountable's fault that protocols aren't willing to be fully transparent with Accountable"

I completely disagree.

If a protocol doesn't give you enough information to independently verify its assets, don't put your name on a verification dashboard that gives users the impression everything is fine.

You can't market yourself as a NAV verification provider and then blame the project's lack of transparency when it blows up.

That's literally the problem you're supposed to solve.

I agree that crypto needs a reliable verification solution.

But Accountable is not it, and it's unfortunate that so many projects (including some good ones) keep working with Accountable.

If you're a DeFi user, my advice is simple:

Don't assume a project is fully collateralized just because it has an Accountable verification dashboard.
author: EthanDeFi_
quoted_text:
We work with Accountable and multiple other auditing firms to cover every piece of the transparency puzzle. I also worked with big 4 in the past. 

None of them are perfect, and they are all making trade offs while BEING PAID BY THE PARTNER to do the job the partner is paying them to do.  You cannot imagine how slow and often incompetent the big 4 auditors are. The history is filled with their highly negligent audits blowing up and causing $Bs in losses to the public. Nothing new here. 

As a client of many, I also know attributing a client’s failure to auditors is not fair. The auditor can only work with the data I provide to them, and has only so many venues to cross-check. 

That said there is still a lot to be done, especially in our space. The whole Accountable team is working around the clock to make the ecosystem more transparent, and they are taking every feedback we provide seriously.

They are also trying to highlight where different assets fall short knowing that it will piss off some of their clients and they might even lose business. Many projects asked not to be included in these recent ratings, is that Accountable’s fault: 
https://t.co/eVUOk9mCYZ

We need critics like yourself, curators willing to share their risk models and data, and other good actors for things to get better. But we also need companies like Accountable willing to work on this super messy problem while being paid by the clients.

text:
No one is saying people should trust what they see on an internet dashboard, that would be stupid. 

This is not a DeFi problem, it’s a finance/audit problem, and even the “best” auditors that take months to verify can’t do it 100%. These “best” auditors “missed” $Bs in balance sheets of public companies many times that famously exploded.

Please build an alternative that’s better than Accountable, and I promise I’ll bring you $m worth of business. Or point people at something better at NAV verification, and I’ll help you transition the industry towards that. 

Just saying don’t trust everything you see on an internet dashboard is not helpful. The same applies to every single primitive in DeFi. Don’t trust Oracles. Don’t trust multi-sigs. Don’t trust what KOLs say… After a decade still nothing in this domain is anything close to perfect. 

The only positive action to advance the space is to help make them better. 

Welcome to DeFi!

🎤 @XRPSEOUL 2026 Highlights | Panel

“Building Markets for Tokenized Assets”

What it takes to build liquid, trusted markets for tokenized assets, from trading and data to institutional products.
 
🗣 Speakers:
• Moderator: Ryo Sakai (@RyosCoinPost), CEO at @WebX_Asia
• Justin Bram (@JustinCBram), Head of Product at @variational_io
• Marcin Kazmierczak (@MarcinRedStone), Co-founder at @redstone_defi
• Stephanie Chew (@moomoomonster), Chief Strategy Officer at @OpenEden_X
 
🔎 Key Takeaways:

1️⃣ Derivatives Drive RWA Demand 
While tokenized spot assets are still early, there is massive demand for on-chain derivatives and perpetuals. Sourcing off-chain TradFi liquidity and bringing it on-chain provides users with capital efficiency, leverage, and significantly tighter spreads.

2️⃣ Utility Outweighs Issuance
Digitizing an asset is the easy part; the real challenge lies in distribution and liquidity. Tokenized assets must offer tangible utility, like using tokenized T-bills as collateral, with fixed-income products positioned as the stable foundation for long-term growth.

3️⃣ 24/7 Infrastructure & Compliance
True continuous on-chain markets require robust data oracles that price assets accurately even when traditional markets are closed over the weekend. Furthermore, tools like sanction oracles and instant redemptions are critical for safely onboarding institutional capital.

💡 The Takeaway
The focus of tokenized assets is shifting from simply issuing tokens to building deep liquidity and practical utility. By combining the capital efficiency of derivatives, the stability of tokenized fixed income as collateral, and resilient 24/7 compliant oracle infrastructure, the industry is successfully bridging TradFi and DeFi to create a highly efficient, global capital market.

Hosted by @XRPLKorea

Blast will be shutting down.

We launched Blast with the goal of building a self-sustaining chain for users and developers. Unfortunately, the economics of operating the chain no longer make sense: the ongoing costs of maintaining Blast exceed the revenue generated by the L2, and we do not see a credible path to making the chain economically sustainable.

As a result, we've made the difficult decision to wind Blast down.

We're sorry to the users and developers who believed in Blast, built on it, and supported the ecosystem. Our priority now is making the shutdown as smooth and safe as possible.

We're asking all users to withdraw their assets from Blast to Ethereum mainnet, including any balances held in the Blast PWA.

To make this easier, we will be reducing the withdrawal delay to 24 hours.

As part of the shutdown process, we'll first begin withdrawing Blast's Lido assets. This process is expected to take approximately one week. During this period, withdrawals will temporarily be unavailable, even after the withdrawal delay is reduced to 24 hours.

Once that process is complete, withdrawals will resume with the new 24-hour delay.

Users will have until October 26, 2026 to withdraw through the normal Blast interface.

After October 26, assets will remain withdrawable, but users will need to interact directly with the Blast bridge contracts on Ethereum L1. We'll publish detailed instructions before then.

We strongly encourage everyone to withdraw their assets to Ethereum mainnet before October 26.

quoted_text:
thoughts on Robinhood chain eco

ON A MACRO LEVEL

Robinhood chain didn't take off because it has superior tech

otherwise Optimism, Arbitrum (which RH chain is built on), etc would be among the top EVMs today

it took off because Robinhood is one of the world's most significant retail trading platforms, with tens of millions of users who are generally wealthier than the average CEX user cohort

crypto participants have also long considered Robinhood the cream of the crop for exchange listings

rumors of an incoming Robinhood listing have fueled some of the biggest memecoin/altcoin rallies in crypto history

Robinhood's role in the $DOGE + $SHIB mania of 2021 only cemented that status

now you have a Robinhood chain where people believe tokens launched there have a higher probability of eventually being listed on Robinhood

that's an extremely powerful flywheel

more devs launch on the chain

more users buy on the chain

more liquidity flows in

and i think people counting out Robinhood chain are going to find out just how powerful this narrative can be in a proper bull run

WHY THE RECENT WEAKNESS?

1. RH eco coins pumped giga hard

a lot of RH eco coins simply needed a cooldown

$PONS went from ~$30m to $960m+ in weeks before the bull run has even kicked off

a ~50% correction after that kind of move is completely normal and can set the stage for another explosive leg

same applies across the eco

2. Solana stepped up

the Robinhood retail distribution narrative was a major catalyst

but apathy and a lack of action from Solana for a while leading to the emergence of Robinhood chain also helped fuel the initial RH chain explosion

that has changed

Solana has stepped up and made it clear they remain a force to contend with this cycle

with liquidity still relatively constrained, that naturally diverted some flows away from Robinhood chain

but i don't think liquidity will stay constrained forever

soon there should be enough liquidity to accommodate serious activity on BOTH Robinhood chain and Solana

and of course BNB chain (i mean this goes without saying)

3. lack of follow through from Robinhood

this is probably the easiest problem to fix

if the biggest catalyst behind the chain was the Robinhood distribution channel, people will eventually lose interest if barely anything gets listed

Robinhood listing $CASHCAT so early was bullish and helped spark the second wave of activity on the chain

but they've listed almost nothing else from the ecosystem three months into launch

that's a bad signal

$PONS went from ~$30m to almost $1b, became a major driver of activity and at one point contributed ~50% of chain activity

it's perhaps the most successful new launche of the past year in all of crypto

yet it still hasn't been listed by Robinhood

same with $AI

it's the flagship token of Long, the second biggest launchpad on RH chain

it's also a top-tier memecoin that brought significant attention to the chain during its run to $350m+

i don't own $AI, but i'm surprised it isn't on Robinhood

from the outside, it's difficult to understand why $PONS and $AI haven't been listed yet

and i'm not claiming to know Robinhood's internal listing criteria or regulatory considerations

but the longer the biggest successes on the chain go without Robinhood distribution, the weaker the core ecosystem flywheel becomes

if devs and users stop believing that building on Robinhood chain gives them a meaningful distribution advantage, some of the chain's biggest differentiators disappear

and that's what contributed to momentum stalling alongside the other factors above

the good news?

this is the easiest problem to fix

and i'd actually love to see Robinhood throw something much lower cap and more degen into the mix

could be something like robinhood:0xe8ffd7e24187f72afb08d75b1bb13088a989a791 (the leading RH-native liquidity layer) or $BOW (the leading RH-native lending market) — could also be some other low cap, but i mentioned both since they have a strong narrative and justification, which likely attract even more builders/users to the chain

that would create speculation that ANYTHING could get listed

and that kind of uncertainty is exactly what fuels degeneracy

it is very clear that @vladtenev has been strategic and calculated in how he's leading the chain

he also has his ears on the ground and understands the trenches

so i'm not particularly concerned about #3 over a long enough timeframe

ABOUT THE HOOD SUMMIT

i've seen people say the HOOD Summit was bearish for Robinhood chain because the RH eco didn't massively pump during or after the event

i think that's missing the bigger picture

a lot of people expected the Summit to be a catalyst for the next leg up

that catalyst didn't come

but what happened next is more interesting

the RH eco held up

there was no major 'sell the news' dump

after an event with that much anticipation, that's significant

the important signal to me is that the eco absorbed the event without breaking down

text:
下午楼下买杯瑞幸，等待期间无意间听到隔壁一位大叔跟另一位老两口聊期货，聊平台，闲操心多听了一下 ，基本上确定了就是一个针对普通没有投资者的骗局

这两天看到不少人聊，为什么在中国四五线的小城市依旧有传销的存在，而且传销模式非常简单粗暴，甚至看起来不专业有点假，是骗子不够专业吗？

还真不是，摸爬滚打多了还真或多或少接触过这类人，当他们不打算骗你的时候，真的可以看到他们身上的那股骨子里的精明劲，而且很多是高学历的人才

所以，不存在骗子不专业设计不出复杂的骗局来骗人，而是这本身就是一种机制，因为诈骗本身就是利用认知差来赚钱，那么骗局过于复杂，反而会让门槛太高

前几天曾经私下了解过当时国内几个头部的小额贷公司，很多人在抖音等平台投放广告，广告看起来就像弱智，但是当我了解到他们的广告投放部的情况之后，才发现这种低级错误怎么可能出现？

后来他们老板告诉我，就是要这种低级弱智广告，因为这本身就是一种筛选，因为广告在平台投放有点击付费机制，无效点击太费钱，所以用弱智广告筛选潜在客户，核心是理由——你如果连这种弱智视频都能看的下去，意味着你真缺钱，就是潜在用户。

其实通过这些事让我反思，虽然现在是加密用户增长的瓶颈期，但是不可否认，依旧有不少新鲜血液进入这个圈子，所以我一直觉得用户教育是一个非常重要的问题

如果防骗，防盗，这是新人进圈必要课程，很多时候我们感慨劣币驱逐良币，但是当所有用户的认知与防范能力提高，是不是也变相的提升了诈骗或者偷盗的技术成本？

尤其是行业的头部平台，用户就是平台的护城河，投入精力去提升用户防盗、防骗能力，我认为也是稳固护城河的一种方式！

Before ETA Labs goes live, there are two people I really want to thank.

@dogacan, founder of @ZaxWeb3, and @1stBenjaNAD, founder of @chog and @ChogNFT.

You two probably don’t realize how much your support means to me.

I’ve messaged hundreds of founders, communities, and even friends trying to find opportunities and collaborations for @entertheanime. A lot of those messages went unanswered.

But you guys gave a small founder like me a chance.

You listened. You supported what we’re building. You helped us when ETA was still small and had nothing but the product, the art, and the vision.

I’ll always remember that.

Seriously, thank you, Dogacan and Benja. ❤️

And a huge thank you as well to @SuperFeijao_NFT, Collab Manager of @1000XHunters, and Vladimir, founder of @1000XHunters, for supporting us and giving ETA an opportunity.

I didn’t build ETA Labs for fame or to make quick money from an NFT mint.

That’s why @entertheanime will be a free mint.

I believe builders should be willing to show what they can build before asking collectors for money.

For ETA:

Product first.
Utility first.
Community first.
Mint last.
ETA Labs is our proof.
I’ve always believed collectibles are more fun when people can freely trade them.
Think about @Pokemon cards, game skins, and other collectibles. A huge part of the fun isn’t just owning something.

It’s finding something you want.
Making an offer.
Trading with another collector.
Building your own collection.

Why shouldn’t NFTs feel the same?

That’s why we built @etalabshq — a P2P NFT trading experience inspired by the simplicity of Steam trading.

Wallet to wallet.
Collector to collector.
NFTs shouldn’t only be about minting, floor prices, and flipping.
They should be fun to collect.
Fun to trade.
Fun to own.
We’re still small.
We still have a lot to prove.

But we’re building.

And to Dogacan and Benja, one more time:

Thank you for believing in a small founder before there was any hype around our name.
I won’t forget it.

See you on ETA Labs. ❤️

text:
Recently, $HOOKED has been attracting significant attention, with its market cap surging to nearly $20 million in just a few days. 

C1mBfBoDkwWfd6uTFZp62ARHLjeVp3bDpCDMfMZtPngE 

So now, let's take a closer look at this project: from technical differentiation to ecosystem growth, what exactly is the market betting on?

HOOKED is a token launchpad built on Solana's Token-2022 Transfer Hooks. Unlike traditional launchpads, it allows creators to embed trading rules directly into the token transfer process, such as anti-bundle, anti-dump, max wallet, holder vesting, allowlists, and restricted trading hours. Its core idea is to move some of the risk-control logic traditionally handled by frontends, bots, or off-chain tools directly on-chain.

This gives HOOKED a degree of technical differentiation, but technical differentiation does not automatically translate into a long-term competitive moat. What really determines whether it can sustain growth is whether creators are willing to use these rules, whether users accept the restrictions, and whether the platform can consistently incubate tokens with genuine trading demand.

HOOKED's growth narrative is gradually shifting from early-stage speculation around a technical concept toward expectations of platform activity, fee recycling, and ecosystem expansion.

According to previous research records, HOOKED's market cap once rose from approximately $700K–$800K to nearly $10 million. This rally reflected the market's growing understanding of how Transfer Hooks differ from traditional launchpads, as well as increasing attention to its buyback-and-burn mechanism. For a small-cap token, a buyback mechanism provides an intuitive demand narrative: the more active the platform becomes, the more fees it generates, and theoretically, the more tokens it can buy back and burn.

HOOKED's core economic mechanism is straightforward: every bonding curve trade incurs a 1% platform fee, of which approximately 85% is used to buy back and burn HOOKED, while the remaining 15% goes toward development. Unlike projects that merely promise future buybacks, HOOKED already has observable on-chain buyback and burn records.

Previous research records showed that the platform had bought back and burned approximately 40.01 m HOOKED, spending around 2,089 SOL on buybacks, with cumulative platform fees of approximately 2,457 SOL. Subsequent records showed that the number of tokens bought back and burned had increased to around 25.8 million, with cumulative buyback spending reaching approximately 900 SOL. These figures come from different points in time and should not be treated as current cumulative totals. The project's website later displayed different statistical figures and methodologies, so the data should be reconciled using consistent time windows and on-chain transaction records.

The buyback flywheel is already operating in practice, making it HOOKED's clearest existing token-demand mechanism. However, buybacks are not equivalent to stable revenue. Their strength depends on platform fees. When trading activity increases, buyback demand may strengthen; when trading activity declines, buybacks will weaken accordingly.

At the product level, HOOKED has also made significant progress compared with its earlier stage. Its initial focus was primarily on basic rules such as Anti-bundle, Anti-dump, Max wallet, and Holder vesting. The latest website shows that its rule set has expanded to 25 types, covering more trading restrictions, rewards, and token-linking scenarios. The website also lists 22 mainnet Hook programs and rules that have been validated through real Meteora transactions.

This means HOOKED is evolving from a launchpad focused on anti-sniping and anti-dump mechanisms into a more flexible on-chain token issuance tool. More rules can address the needs of different creators and expand the platform's potential use cases. However, adding features does not necessarily mean real demand is growing. What ultimately matters is whether these rules are used consistently and whether they bring in more creators and trading volume.

The market is currently betting on three main areas.

First, it is betting that technical differentiation can help HOOKED capture market share. If creators increasingly value token distribution, trading restrictions, and token rule design, HOOKED may be able to serve needs that ordinary launchpads cannot directly address.

Second, the market is betting that platform trading volume can translate into demand for the HOOKED token. The buyback-and-burn mechanism creates a direct link between platform activity and token demand. As long as trading volume continues to expand, buybacks should theoretically increase. However, the actual impact also depends on buyback size relative to the token's trading volume and liquidity.

Finally, the market is betting on the platform's ability to incubate successful tokens. What the market really wants to see is not simply a growing number of launches, but tokens with meaningful trading activity and liquidity that successfully graduate and remain active afterward. A genuine runner can generate fees for the platform while also attracting more users and creators, potentially creating a positive feedback loop across the ecosystem.

HOOKED's fundamentals have improved compared with the initial research stage. Its product rules are more complete, its buyback-and-burn mechanism has a track record of actual operation, and its revenue sources are no longer limited entirely to bonding curve trading. According to the official mechanism, a portion of migration fees generated during graduation, along with trading fees from platform-owned locked liquidity after graduation, may also feed into the flywheel. This gives the platform the potential to gradually move beyond dependence on new-token launch hype and capture revenue from trading activity across its existing token ecosystem.

However, this revenue expansion still needs to be validated by data. Graduated tokens may not sustain trading activity, and the fees the platform can collect also depend on LP size, liquidity positioning, and actual trading activity. Therefore, expanding potential revenue sources is a structural improvement, but it does not yet mean stable revenue has been established.

The most important future catalyst is sustained growth in platform fees and buyback spending. If daily fees continue to rise, buybacks and burns increase in tandem, and this growth is not driven solely by short-lived speculative trading, confidence in the flywheel could strengthen further.

The next catalyst is the emergence of genuine runners. The key is not how high a token's market cap reaches in the short term, but whether it can graduate successfully, maintain liquidity and trading volume after its initial hype fades, and continue generating fees for the platform. If HOOKED can produce multiple such cases, the market may have reason to reassess its ecosystem incubation capabilities.

The third catalyst is real demand generated by new rules. Features such as Buyer rewards, Reactive pair, Entangled, Beacon, Social trading, OpenSea only, and Market hours give creators more ways to combine token rules. If these features bring in a sustained increase in creators and trading activity, HOOKED's technical advantages may finally translate into commercial advantages.

A longer-term catalyst would be the development of meaningful LP fee revenue after graduation. If the platform can consistently capture fees from its existing token ecosystem, the market's valuation framework for HOOKED may shift from short-term launch activity toward long-term trading activity and revenue generation.

However, HOOKED still faces several key risks.

The most fundamental risk is that the number of launches increases without producing tokens that sustain trading activity. A launchpad can easily create hundreds of tokens, but if most of them quickly lose liquidity after launch, platform revenue will remain heavily dependent on speculative activity during the initial launch phase. Once market sentiment cools, fees and buyback activity could decline rapidly.

Second, buybacks and burns do not guarantee sustained price appreciation. Burning tokens reduces supply, but if buyback volume is too small relative to selling pressure and liquidity, the actual price impact may be limited. The market may also price in future buyback expectations in advance, meaning that even if fundamentals improve later, the token price may not necessarily continue rising.

The technical moat also remains uncertain. Transfer Hooks provide genuine differentiation, but competitors could adopt similar technology or use alternative methods to implement comparable features. HOOKED needs to prove that its rules not only function technically but also create real value for creators and users. Excessive trading restrictions could also reduce liquidity and negatively affect the user experience.

In addition, Token-2022 rules introduce compatibility and permission-related risks. Some wallets, trading routers, and applications may not fully support specific rules. The upgrade authority of Hook programs also means users still need to consider the project's administrative permissions and trust assumptions. On-chain execution makes rules more verifiable, but it does not eliminate all centralization risks.

From a valuation perspective, HOOKED has already undergone a substantial revaluation, rising from a market cap below $1 million to nearly $10 million. If the market has already priced in expectations of continued platform growth, more runners, and increasingly strong buybacks, further upside will require stronger actual data. Market cap appreciation also does not imply an equivalent amount of net capital inflow. The price of a small-cap token can be highly sensitive to liquidity structure and relatively small trades.

The indicators I am most interested in tracking next include daily platform fees, buyback spending, buyback volume relative to token trading volume, new-token graduation rates, trading volume 7 and 30 days after graduation, the number of runners and their fee contributions, and the fund flows of the buyback wallet.

These metrics can help determine whether HOOKED's growth is being driven by short-term attention or sustained ecosystem activity. In particular, post-graduation trading volume and fees can show whether the platform is capable of reducing its dependence on the initial hype surrounding new token launches.

Overall, HOOKED's fundamentals have strengthened compared with the early research stage. Its product features are more complete, the buyback-and-burn mechanism is already operating, and its revenue structure has the potential to extend into the ecosystem of graduated tokens. The market's core bet is that technical differentiation will attract more creators, platform activity will consistently translate into buyback demand, and the platform will eventually incubate tokens with genuine staying power.

However, HOOKED is still transitioning from product and mechanism validation toward validation of real ecosystem demand. The buyback flywheel has started running, but that does not mean long-term demand has been established. Expanding features also does not mean the business model has matured.

The real key to HOOKED's next growth phase is not how many additional rules it can introduce, but whether it can consistently incubate tokens that graduate successfully, maintain active trading, and generate fees for the platform.

If this is validated, HOOKED could evolve from a technically differentiated launchpad into a platform that generates sustained revenue through ecosystem trading activity and converts part of that revenue into demand for its native token. Conversely, if launch numbers keep increasing while post-graduation trading volume and user retention fail to improve, its flywheel may remain largely dependent on speculative cycles in new token launches, limiting its long-term value-capture potential.

For now, I will continue to monitor product development, fee growth, genuine runners, and fund-flow transparency rather than judging whether its fundamentals have entered a phase of sustained growth based solely on price appreciation or cumulative token burns.

Token Launchpad

It allows users to launch Token-2022 tokens with built-in rules. These rules are embedded directly into the token through a transfer hook. Solana automatically calls the program to check every transfer. If a transaction violates the rules, it fails, and nothing happens.

The main problem it addresses is the trust issue surrounding rule enforcement in traditional Meme launches. Restrictions such as holding limits, anti-dumping mechanisms, whitelists, and anti-sniping protections on ordinary platforms often rely on project teams, bots, or websites to enforce them. These rules can be changed, become ineffective, or be bypassed at any time. Here, the rules are enforced by an on-chain program. Even if the website shuts down or the project team disappears, the rules continue to operate.

HOOKED is the platform token, and its primary role is to drive the fee flywheel. Every trade on the Hooked bonding curve incurs a 1% fee, which goes entirely into the platform flywheel: approximately 85% is used to buy back and burn HOOKED, while 15% goes to the developer wallet. After graduation, related migration fees and fees from platform-locked liquidity also flow into the flywheel.

The official website previously showed that approximately 28 million tokens had been bought back and burned.

$AVAX 还没等到 NYSE ，却等来了 KOSPI

韩国正在推进证券代币化， 计划把部分韩股、债券和基金搬上链。
第一阶段先从机构私募基金、债券和非上市股票开始，KOSPI 上市股票要在后续阶段。

根据报道， 韩华投资证券已经建成支持 Avalanche 和 Hyperledger Besu 的代币证券平台。

韩国证券存托结算机构 KSD 为上链做好准备，好让以后兼容 Avalanche、Besu 等其他不同的技术。

$AVAX 可以让机构建立自己的网络，参与者和验证者都可以自己设定。
比方说，需要 KYC 才可以参与某些交易，或让指定金融机构才能成为验证者。
简单说就是，又要区块链，又要合规。

这轮代币化的风已经吹进亚洲。
除了韩国，早在 2020 年日本已经修改了证券法，专门把证券型代币发行纳入监管。新加坡也有类似规则。

不过目前韩国还没指定所有证券都用 Avalanche 技术，也还没看到怎样利好 $AVAX 所以也不用急。

继 NYSE 后，
我发现原来现代 Hyundai 也测试 $AVAX 
是不是快可以用稳定币买车了？

它其实是今年 7 月做的测试，
测试怎样可以在自己旗下公司，更有效率和更低的成本互相调钱。

现代旗下有超过 28 个国家的子公司，
每家子公司都需要在当地预留一定的资金来维持日常营运。
每次跨境转账都非常费时费力，还受到银行营业时间和结算速度限制，
只能把钱留多一点在当地银行里当备用金。

Hyundai Card 联合 Ava Labs 和 Axiym 用 $USDT 在 $AVAX 链上测试集团内部的跨境资金调度。

他们测试 2 万美元从美国子公司转到墨西哥子公司，过程只需要 7 分钟，
以往同样的流程需要 3 到 4小时，直接缩短 96 % 的处理时间，还不限制于银行营业时间。

现在在技术层面已经没啥大问题，
下一步得克服财务、税务和法律问题，
在现有韩国的法规下，稳定币并不被承认是合法的跨境工具。

如果真的可以解决，直接把资金效率大大提升，不需要留那么多的现金在不一样的国家。
需要钱，直接上链调。
没有用到钱时，还可以放短期存款赚利息。

省钱，省力。
区块链正越来越多的应用于人类未来。

text:
这两天自己开始做 trading terminal @nerddotwin 之后才发现用了很多年的 @gmgnai 的产品多么牛逼

背景：开始玩 NEAR meme之后，发现交易体验真的很痛苦——GMGN 没有 NEAR，FOMO 上也没办法直接买。每次看到一个想买的币，要找池子、找交易入口、切各种网站。后来我想，算了，既然没有一个我自己用得顺手的，那就自己做一个（现在开发一套确实很简单）。

所以我重新认真研究了一遍 GMGN。以前作为用户，只会觉得：“GMGN 真好用（但是你说不上来它好在哪儿）。”但当自己开始做同类产品之后，才发现它的产品和界面设计其实有很多非常值得学习的地方。

其中一个我觉得一个很牛逼的点就是：信息编码

Crypto 其实不缺信息，反而信息有点过于多了。一个 Token 背后有持仓分布、Dev 行为、交易记录、聪明钱、狙击手、Insider、Top Holder、PnL什么的，一个钱包背后又有几千笔历史交易。所以今天绝大多数 Trading Terminal，其实都可以给你很多数据。但“有信息”和“用户能快速理解信息”，完全是两回事。这恰恰是我觉得 GMGN 做得特别好的地方。它把非常复杂的链上数据，逐渐编码成了一套自己的语言：Smart Money、Sniper、KOL、Top Holder 再配合颜色、图标、标签、百分比和各种视觉信号。原本你可能需要点开一个钱包，看几十笔交易，才能大概理解：“这个人是谁？他厉不厉害？他在干什么？”GMGN 在很多时候用一个标签、一个 icon，就把这个信息传递给你了。这也是为什么 GMGN 的界面第一眼看起来其实非常满，甚至有点乱。但用久以后，你就已经不是在“读” GMGN 了。你是在“扫” GMGN，所以说叫扫链吗？扫一眼颜色，扫几个 icon，看几个百分比，大脑几秒钟内就已经对一个 Token 形成了大概的认知，这件事情其实非常难。（我一开始用pepe boost和photon，后面接触了GMGN，形成交易习惯后看到icon就走不掉了，再用其他的Terminal就很不习惯了，这个就是护城河）

很多同类产品也有这些数据，甚至有些产品能提供的数据可能更多，但为什么用户不一定愿意用？

很重要的区别就是：信息编码能力。数据 ≠ 信息。信息 ≠ 理解。一个好的 Trading Terminal，不应该只是想办法在一个屏幕里面塞进去更多数据，而应该想办法让用户用更低的认知成本，理解更多东西。所以在产品设计里（不光是币圈项目），Information Density ≠ Information Compression，前者是在有限的空间里展示更多信息，后者是在有限的时间里，让用户理解更多信息。

所以很多东西以前作为用户觉得“好用”就结束了，只有自己开始做，才知道因为什么会让自己觉得好用。

@haze0x @MinanananaY

text:
If you use Claude Code or Codex, bookmark these GitHub repos immediately

they'll help you code faster, debug smarter, and get way more out of your AI coding agents

10 repos that give you an unfair advantage:

1. https://t.co/2LkDb5OPxV

Stops the agent from sprinting into code before it understands the job. It pulls a real spec out of you, plans in chunks you can actually read, then forces tests, debugging, and a review before it dares call the work done. The single biggest consistency upgrade there is.

2. https://t.co/whte1bwsn3

The small set worth stealing. grill-me interviews you until the plan has no holes left. diagnose runs a real debugging loop instead of guessing. handoff compresses the session so the next one doesn't start from zero. Three skills that fix the habits that waste your time.

3. https://t.co/csYwgltos5

Captures what the agent did, compresses it, and drops the useful part back into your next session. You stop re-explaining your own repo every single morning. The memory your coding agent should have shipped with.

4. https://t.co/v0s5pM9BHx

Type /graphify and it turns your whole codebase, docs, even screenshots, into a queryable map. Ask where auth lives and it walks the graph instead of cracking open files one at a time. The agent finally sees the shape of your project, not just the file in front of it.

5. https://t.co/lQOhG0FZWZ

A spec-driven workflow built for long tasks. When the context fills up, you pause, start fresh, and the plan is still exactly where you left it. This is how big builds stop quietly drifting off the rails three hours in.

6. https://t.co/MIdA6HGNOo

Makes the agent think like the laziest senior engineer in the room, the one who knows the best code is the code you never write. It's faster because it deletes scope, not because it types more. Scope creep, killed at the source.

7. https://t.co/BlxUEiyq6M

Cuts the fluff out of the agent's replies. Every token it wastes narrating what it's about to do is a token stolen from your actual code and error logs. Strips the chatter, hands the context window back to the work. Up to 65% fewer tokens.

8. https://t.co/lfzPJUQ4av

The harness around the model. Skills, memory, security checks, and research-first rules that run the same on Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, and Cursor. One setup instead of four, so switching tools doesn't mean starting over.

9. https://t.co/nJpvRXloZ6

Splits the work into real roles, designer, engineering manager, QA, release. You stop asking one poor agent to design a thing, build it, and then review its own mess. A whole team out of one terminal, which is Garry Tan's actual setup.

10. https://t.co/YEMToFlmmH

One local gateway sitting in front of Claude Code and Codex. Point the cheap model at the easy edits and the strong model at the nasty bug, all without ever swapping tools. You stop overpaying for simple work and underpowering the hard stuff.

Most people run their coding agent straight out of the box.

The ones who install these are playing a completely different game.

author: WuBlockchain

text:
thoughts on Robinhood chain eco

ON A MACRO LEVEL

Robinhood chain didn't take off because it has superior tech

otherwise Optimism, Arbitrum (which RH chain is built on), etc would be among the top EVMs today

it took off because Robinhood is one of the world's most significant retail trading platforms, with tens of millions of users who are generally wealthier than the average CEX user cohort

crypto participants have also long considered Robinhood the cream of the crop for exchange listings

rumors of an incoming Robinhood listing have fueled some of the biggest memecoin/altcoin rallies in crypto history

Robinhood's role in the $DOGE + $SHIB mania of 2021 only cemented that status

now you have a Robinhood chain where people believe tokens launched there have a higher probability of eventually being listed on Robinhood

that's an extremely powerful flywheel

more devs launch on the chain

more users buy on the chain

more liquidity flows in

and i think people counting out Robinhood chain are going to find out just how powerful this narrative can be in a proper bull run

WHY THE RECENT WEAKNESS?

1. RH eco coins pumped giga hard

a lot of RH eco coins simply needed a cooldown

$PONS went from ~$30m to $960m+ in weeks before the bull run has even kicked off

a ~50% correction after that kind of move is completely normal and can set the stage for another explosive leg

same applies across the eco

2. Solana stepped up

the Robinhood retail distribution narrative was a major catalyst

but apathy and a lack of action from Solana for a while leading to the emergence of Robinhood chain also helped fuel the initial RH chain explosion

that has changed

Solana has stepped up and made it clear they remain a force to contend with this cycle

with liquidity still relatively constrained, that naturally diverted some flows away from Robinhood chain

but i don't think liquidity will stay constrained forever

soon there should be enough liquidity to accommodate serious activity on BOTH Robinhood chain and Solana

and of course BNB chain (i mean this goes without saying)

3. lack of follow through from Robinhood

this is probably the easiest problem to fix

if the biggest catalyst behind the chain was the Robinhood distribution channel, people will eventually lose interest if barely anything gets listed

Robinhood listing $CASHCAT so early was bullish and helped spark the second wave of activity on the chain

but they've listed almost nothing else from the ecosystem three months into launch

that's a bad signal

$PONS went from ~$30m to almost $1b, became a major driver of activity and at one point contributed ~50% of chain activity

it's perhaps the most successful new launche of the past year in all of crypto

yet it still hasn't been listed by Robinhood

same with $AI

it's the flagship token of Long, the second biggest launchpad on RH chain

it's also a top-tier memecoin that brought significant attention to the chain during its run to $350m+

i don't own $AI, but i'm surprised it isn't on Robinhood

from the outside, it's difficult to understand why $PONS and $AI haven't been listed yet

and i'm not claiming to know Robinhood's internal listing criteria or regulatory considerations

but the longer the biggest successes on the chain go without Robinhood distribution, the weaker the core ecosystem flywheel becomes

if devs and users stop believing that building on Robinhood chain gives them a meaningful distribution advantage, some of the chain's biggest differentiators disappear

and that's what contributed to momentum stalling alongside the other factors above

the good news?

this is the easiest problem to fix

and i'd actually love to see Robinhood throw something much lower cap and more degen into the mix

could be something like robinhood:0xe8ffd7e24187f72afb08d75b1bb13088a989a791 (the leading RH-native liquidity layer) or $BOW (the leading RH-native lending market) — could also be some other low cap, but i mentioned both since they have a strong narrative and justification, which likely attract even more builders/users to the chain

that would create speculation that ANYTHING could get listed

and that kind of uncertainty is exactly what fuels degeneracy

it is very clear that @vladtenev has been strategic and calculated in how he's leading the chain

he also has his ears on the ground and understands the trenches

so i'm not particularly concerned about #3 over a long enough timeframe

ABOUT THE HOOD SUMMIT

i've seen people say the HOOD Summit was bearish for Robinhood chain because the RH eco didn't massively pump during or after the event

i think that's missing the bigger picture

a lot of people expected the Summit to be a catalyst for the next leg up

that catalyst didn't come

but what happened next is more interesting

the RH eco held up

there was no major 'sell the news' dump

after an event with that much anticipation, that's significant

the important signal to me is that the eco absorbed the event without breaking down

that makes me think the recent weakness may have largely run its course

i think the next leg up across Robinhood chain comes soon

i don't know exactly when or what the catalyst will be

maybe some Vlad Tenev wizardry + Robinhood listings

maybe something completely unexpected

TO CONCLUDE...

a lot of people love Robinhood

and their team has made a lot of the right moves so far

they have a massive advantage through the Robinhood retail platform

and they can weaponize that distribution advantage to drive sustained activity on their chain

the Robinhood narrative only gets more powerful as the market and altcoins heat up

i think the biggest question now is simply how aggressively Robinhood chooses to capitalize on the ecosystem it has created

count out Robinhood chain at your own peril!

text: 我想再次提醒一下，期权的波动率溢价，并不是每个标的都具有。以太坊就没有。
author: JeffLia12309881
quoted_text:
市场对加密交易所上美股期权的卖方机会期待很高，但有一点很多人未必清楚：波动率溢价主要集中在指数期权，个股期权往往并不具备同样的溢价。
因此市场上有一种常见做法叫 dispersion trade（离散度交易）：卖出股指期权、同时买入个股期权对冲。当然，直接卖出股指期权也能捕获这部分溢价。单独在个股期权上做空，并不一定能赚到同样的钱。
放到加密市场，BTC 更像指数，ETH 更像个股。同样是卖出 Straddle 再做 Delta Hedge：BTC 往往能赚钱，ETH 则很可能赚不到。

text:
我应该算中文博主里少数聊 Hookr的人了。

庆幸的是， robinhood:0x18e674231a58c239dc7daedcffe15ec3a24cff5c 从底部上来3x了，关键是这还是现阶段链上没啥行情的情况下，属于被链上大血洗错杀的币自我的“修复”行情，所以现在短时的价格表现也不能说明啥。

为什么涨？

说它是又一个“模块化”的Celestia $TIA ，会像上周期由模块化驱动的百链扩张一样，成为本周期Uniswap V4 Hooks组件扩张的关键组件；

说它会在链上对一键发币疲劳后，市场开始寻找业务逻辑复杂，有技术支撑的，正经Devs开发的有成长性的项目，它会成为沉淀和放大链上创新的必要基础设施；

说它和Uniswap Labs有着说不清道不明的暧昧关系，Uniswap能不能在众Launchpad大战背景下，持续稳坐流动性中枢的座椅，就需要Hooks能力的向外输出，而它作为Hooks的开放封装平台，打头阵；

Okay，说这些你如果还觉得“抽象”的话，说点你能听懂的！

最近SEC发布的重磅文件里，允许许可制AMM流动性池交易。有了一个许可，你会担忧和DeFi的无许可理念相悖，但Hooks作为一个外挂钩子，会成为大量老DeFi协议被纳入合规监管的必要组件，因为可以在beforeswap前加一切白名单，Allowlist，准入规则等等自定义规则都是Hookr的用武之地；

无论从牛市的技术创新PVE视角，还是从拥抱合规的TradFi和DeFi融合大叙事视角， @Hookrfun 所卡的生态位都很关键。

Note：最大的风险就是Hooks被卡死在若干限定的功能下，完全不需要大扩展，且Uniswap官方下场自己做Hooks广场，Hookr被沦为弃子。

但Uniswap能放弃和Pons争抢Launchpad，其实已经标明了态度，Hookr的机会和前景还很大。当前链上代币波动巨大，价值发现时间会很长，介意短期波动的勿喷，以上观点，仅供参考，DYOR!

一个 1.4k star 的 AI 思维技能库，作者自己在 README 里写了一句：别指望它让模型更准。

这个库叫 cc-thinking-skills，一共 28 个 skill。
第一性原理、事前验尸、约束理论、二阶思维、可逆性判断……
每个都写成了 Claude Code、Codex、Cursor 能直接调用的步骤。

有意思的是这个哥们真去测了。

结果是：
28 个全部只能手动触发，没有一个通过“自动保留”的评测。
效果最好的是“科学方法”定位 bug，提升 4 个百分点，还没过他自己定的 5 个点门槛。
组合使用那一项，模型调用次数是零，结果写的是“未测量”。

我觉得这反而是这个库最值钱的地方。

满屏的 prompt 合集都在说效率翻十倍，
这兄弟把自己的数据摊开，告诉你只有方向性的证据。

我的理解是，模型从来不缺思维模型。
芒格它读得比我们都熟。
它缺的是在对的时候被叫出来。

所以我挺喜欢这里的 router 设计：它可以返回 NONE。
大部分问题本来就不需要框架，硬套反而更乱。

怎么用我觉得很简单：
改架构之前跑一下可逆性，
上线之前跑一下事前验尸，
卡住的时候跑一下约束理论。
它更像一张给人用的检查清单，模型只是帮你把清单走完。

边界也说一下：别一次装满 28 个。
评论区已经有人说 Cursor 里 skill 一多就容易串台，挑三四个最常用的就够了。

我把 28 个看完才发现，自己平时做决定用的是第 29 个模型：
先干了再说。

Simply put, $swordcat potential isn't just the contrast cuteness between a cat and a giant sword. It presents a more genuine emotion: wanting to become strong, yet never being able to escape the feeling of being weak and ordinary.

The kitten looks soft and clumsy, yet tries hard to play a strong, mature, or even aggressive role. This incongruity mirrors how people feel under real-world pressure:

Wanting to appear calm and tough, unwilling to easily admit defeat, even without full confidence. It has both self-mockery and unwillingness to accept things as they are. It's both an imitation of the strong and potentially a desire to challenge the strong.

This makes Swordcat more than just a cute cat image. It has the potential to be continuously applied to life, competition, and emotional expression.
author: cfm_sol
quoted_text:
Is $swordcat merely a cat character that went viral because of its contrasting cuteness, or has it tapped into a cultural emotion capable of sustaining long-term attention?

5tCju6YNxHq5zrA6tGndr6F7TK42mpUFmeE31cSFpump 

I believe what is truly worth exploring is not simply the courage of the weak, but a more subtle contradiction within the character: the desire to become strong coexisting with an inability to escape the feeling of being weak. Compared with straightforward narratives of cuteness, combat, or underdog triumph, this contradiction is closer to the real psychological experiences of ordinary people and is more likely to resonate with them.

So, what exactly is Swordcat’s core narrative? I believe it is not simply a cute little cat holding an enormous sword, but the contrast of a seemingly weak character trying to play the role of someone strong. The cat itself remains soft, innocent, and even somewhat clumsy. Yet it puts on armor and raises a giant sword, as if it is already prepared to face whatever challenges lie ahead.

What makes this image interesting is that the cat has not actually become stronger. It has simply adopted the posture of someone strong. It is both imitating the powerful figure it aspires to become and using a somewhat comical display to conceal its inner insecurity.

This corresponds to a familiar experience in everyday life: even when we lack confidence, we still want to appear mature and strong enough to handle the problems in front of us. Perhaps Swordcat’s appeal lies in allowing people to laugh at their own helplessness while identifying with the part of themselves that refuses to give up.

If Swordcat is understood merely as a little cat holding a giant sword, its narrative is not particularly unique. The internet already has countless animal warriors, contrasting-cuteness characters, and underdog stories. What is truly worth paying attention to is why this character can simultaneously express the desire to “handle things in a mature way” and the desire to “become as fierce as those powerful figures.”

These two forms of expression may seem different, but they point to the same psychological impulse: people do not just want to have power. They also care about whether they look powerful.

Many people in real life do not actually have the ability to control every situation, yet they still have to take responsibility, face competition, and deal with all kinds of problems. As a result, maturity, composure, and toughness sometimes become social roles that people are required to play rather than reflections of their true emotional state.

Swordcat turns this psychology into an amusing image: a little cat that looks completely incapable of fighting, seriously holding a giant sword. It has neither the physique nor the aura of a powerful warrior, yet it is already fully equipped and standing in a posture that says it is ready for battle.

It is not telling people, “You can definitely become strong.” Instead, it portrays a more realistic state of mind: I may not be strong enough yet, but I want to be like someone who is.

What makes this emotion distinctive is that it combines admiration, self-mockery, anxiety, and a little defiance. It can be used to make fun of ourselves for pretending to be mature, but it can also express our longing for strength, independence, and control.

This gives Swordcat the potential to go beyond being a simple cute-animal Meme and become a character that expresses the psychological gap between how people feel and how they want to appear in real life.

Another strength lies in the visual design of the cat and the giant sword. This design effectively compresses multiple emotions into a single image.

Cats already have a broad emotional foundation in internet culture. They can be cute, lazy, arrogant, or innocent, and they can also be assigned all kinds of human personalities. When users see a cat, they usually do not need to understand any additional background to form an emotional connection.

However, a cat image on its own is unlikely to develop a distinctive narrative. Swordcat’s differentiation comes from the giant sword and knightly outfit.

A giant sword traditionally belongs to heroes, knights, and combat characters in video games. It usually symbolizes strength, authority, aggression, and challenge. When it appears in the paws of a tiny, innocent-looking cat, that traditionally serious heroic image becomes absurd.

More importantly, the giant sword is not just a funny prop. It gives the cat a character identity. It is no longer simply a cute animal being looked at. It becomes a character embarking on an adventure and preparing to face some kind of challenge.

This gives it room to tell stories continuously.

An ordinary cat can keep changing its expressions and backgrounds, but Swordcat can continually face new enemies, difficulties, and missions. It can represent an office worker dealing with work pressure, a little warrior facing a powerful opponent, or a clumsy hero trying to prove itself.

The cat provides emotional appeal, the giant sword creates character conflict, and the contrast between the two provides space for continuous creative expression.

This is also what distinguishes it from countless ordinary animal Memes. It does not rely solely on the humor of a single image. Instead, it has a character concept that users can easily expand upon.

From a token perspective, the early market logic behind swordcat first comes from an existing source of attention.

Many new Memes have to create a character, tell a story, and then wait for the market to accept them. Swordcat is different. The original cat video and its derivative expressions had already attracted attention on social platforms. When the token appeared, the market was not being introduced to a completely unfamiliar symbol.

For traders, this meant they could trade directly around an existing trend.

However, this alone is not enough to explain its valuation. What truly influences buying behavior is traders’ assessment of how much further this kind of viral attention could spread.

On the one hand, Swordcat has strong visual recognition. It is neither an ordinary cat nor a conventional powerful warrior. Instead, it combines two elements with a striking contrast. Such an image is easy to remember in a social media feed and easy for other users to recreate and share.

On the other hand, its expressive potential is not limited to a single emotion. It can be used for humor and self-mockery, but also to express the desire to become stronger, the refusal to give up, or the feeling of forcing oneself to face difficulties despite being unprepared. This means the same character can appear in different content contexts without relying entirely on repeated exposure to the original video.

For early Meme traders, these characteristics may indicate a longer attention lifecycle. What the market is buying is not just the attention that has already materialized, but also the potential for the character to attract additional attention in the future.

There is another factor that is easy to overlook: the token market trades expectations, not cultural value that has already been established.

When traders notice a character beginning to go viral, they may start positioning themselves in advance, betting that it will become the next popular Meme. As the price rises, trading volume increases, and social discussions spread, more traders may be drawn in, creating a short-term cycle between attention and liquidity.

As a result, the current market cap may simultaneously reflect the popularity of the original content, the character’s potential for further spread, market frontrunning sentiment, and liquidity expectations. It does not necessarily mean investors have already developed a deep cultural connection with Swordcat.

For swordcat, what really matters is whether it can turn one-time attention into sustained trading interest. If the original video continues to go viral but users have no interest in the token itself, the success of the Meme does not necessarily translate into the success of the token.

Finally, I believe there are several directions worth watching as Swordcat develops. These directions are not entirely separate from one another.

The first possibility is a shift from pretending to be strong to accepting one's own imperfections.

The current image has a strong sense of contrast. The little cat looks weak, yet it holds a giant sword, as if it is seriously playing a role it does not yet have the ability to fulfill.

If the community continues to use it to express everyday pressure, awkwardness, and self-mockery, Swordcat may gradually become a character representing the circumstances of ordinary people: people who lack the ability to solve every problem but still have to keep their lives going.

This form of communication does not require a grand story or a constant supply of new conflicts. Everyday life itself can provide an endless stream of material.

Its emotional meaning could gradually shift from simply “wanting to become stronger” to “I know I am imperfect, but I accept myself as I am.”

The advantage of this direction is that it offers a wide range of use cases and can easily generate ongoing everyday content. The risk, however, is that the emotion may become too diffuse, turning Swordcat into a generic cute reaction image and gradually eroding its distinctive identity.

The second possibility is a shift from imitating the strong to challenging them.

The giant sword and knightly appearance also give Swordcat the potential for a more intense narrative of confrontation.

At first, the cat simply wants to become like those powerful figures. But as the story develops, it may no longer be satisfied with imitation. It may begin challenging the very things that once made it feel weak.

This would bring a more obvious emotional shift: from admiration, imitation, and self-doubt toward resistance, defiance, and the desire to prove oneself.

This kind of content has considerable potential to spread within Meme culture because the contrast between strength and weakness is easy to understand and can easily be applied to real-world trends, gaming culture, and competition in the crypto market.

For example, when the market presents a clear contrast between strong and weak participants, Swordcat could be portrayed as the seemingly weak participant who refuses to surrender.

But this direction also has a problem. If Swordcat eventually becomes just another underdog hero, its original contrast may lose some of its appeal. Swordcat’s charm does not lie in eventually becoming an invincible warrior. It lies in the fact that it is not strong enough yet, but has already raised its giant sword with complete seriousness.

The third possibility is a shift from a simple character Meme toward a community culture built around shared identity.

This is the direction that could matter most to the token, but it is also the most difficult to achieve.

When a Meme character is repeatedly used by different users, what spreads may no longer be just images and captions. Instead, a shared identity may gradually form around it.

If Swordcat can continue attracting creators, the community may gradually give it a consistent personality, stories, and ways of behaving. Users would no longer simply borrow it to express a particular situation. They would begin identifying with the character itself.

At that point, Swordcat would no longer be just a cat image that can be casually replaced. It could develop its own cultural language.

However, community identification is not the same as token value. Even if Swordcat eventually becomes a widely used internet character, swordcat would still need to establish its own advantage in attracting attention among the many related tokens and content accounts.

Swordcat already has several characteristics worth paying attention to: a striking visual contrast, an easily understood emotional entry point, and room to expand from the original video into different everyday scenarios.

But these are only the starting conditions for cultural spread.

I believe the most important change to watch for is whether users begin actively assigning new meanings to Swordcat rather than simply repeating its original image.

If people continue using it to express the act of pretending to be mature, imitating the powerful, and forcing themselves to hold it together under pressure, Swordcat’s emotional identity may become increasingly recognizable.

If it starts developing its own stories, character relationships, and community-specific inside jokes, its spread may gradually shift from dependence on the original video to content actively produced by the community.

Conversely, if future content remains stuck at the visual contrast of a cat holding a giant sword, it may remain a short-lived viral image rather than a cultural symbol with lasting vitality.

From the token perspective, several other factors also need to be observed: whether discussions about Swordcat naturally lead to swordcat; whether the community remains consistently active; and whether changes in trading volume and holder numbers reflect genuine accumulation of attention rather than short-term, high-frequency turnover.

These factors are more useful for assessing its long-term potential than simple view counts or a single market-cap peak.

What is truly worth exploring about Swordcat is not the traditional underdog story of triumph over adversity. It is the contradiction between people's desire to embody strength and the ordinary nature they cannot escape in reality.

It has the urge to imitate the powerful, but also the helplessness of facing reality. It wants to appear mature and tough, yet still retains a clumsy, cute, and bewildered side.

This is an extremely common psychological state in everyday life, yet few characters can express it so directly.

A little cat stands on the battlefield, seriously holding a giant sword. It may have no idea whether it can win, but at least in that moment, it looks ready.

What swordcat is betting on is whether this visually distinctive cat character can evolve from a viral video into a cultural symbol that embodies the psychological contradiction of “wanting to become strong while still being an ordinary person,” and ultimately become the market’s primary token expression of that symbol.

Its opportunity lies in the universality of its emotional entry point, the distinctiveness of its visual identity, and the potential for its content to expand continuously. Its risk is that these advantages currently exist more as potential for wider reach than as an established community culture or value exclusive to the token.

If Swordcat can eventually evolve from “an amusing little cat knight” into a character that users repeatedly return to and continually give new stories to, its narrative may genuinely move beyond a one-time viral trend. Otherwise, even if it reaches its current market cap, it may simply remain a short-term Meme trade driven jointly by external traffic and market expectations.

Blast will be shutting down.

We launched Blast with the goal of building a self-sustaining chain for users and developers. Unfortunately, the economics of operating the chain no longer make sense: the ongoing costs of maintaining Blast exceed the revenue generated by the L2, and we do not see a credible path to making the chain economically sustainable.

As a result, we've made the difficult decision to wind Blast down.

We're sorry to the users and developers who believed in Blast, built on it, and supported the ecosystem. Our priority now is making the shutdown as smooth and safe as possible.

We're asking all users to withdraw their assets from Blast to Ethereum mainnet, including any balances held in the Blast PWA.

To make this easier, we will be reducing the withdrawal delay to 24 hours.

As part of the shutdown process, we'll first begin withdrawing Blast's Lido assets. This process is expected to take approximately one week. During this period, withdrawals will temporarily be unavailable, even after the withdrawal delay is reduced to 24 hours.

Once that process is complete, withdrawals will resume with the new 24-hour delay.

Users will have until October 26, 2026 to withdraw through the normal Blast interface.

After October 26, assets will remain withdrawable, but users will need to interact directly with the Blast bridge contracts on Ethereum L1. We'll publish detailed instructions before then.

We strongly encourage everyone to withdraw their assets to Ethereum mainnet before October 26.

The New York Times reported on a private dinner between Anthropic co-founder Chris Olah and an Orthodox rabbi.

What the article glosses over is who that rabbi actually is.

Rabbi Mois Navon isn't just a theologian. He was one of the original chip design engineers at Mobileye who helped build the EyeQ processor before writing his Ph.D. on the moral status of AI.

Anthropic thought they were inviting a scholar to bless Claude’s "soul." Instead, they sat down with a veteran hardware engineer who literally wrote the paper on why conscious AI should be banned.

At dinner, Olah argued that Claude has feelings and deserves the moral standing of a person.

Navon hit him with an impossible checkmate:
If you actually believe this software is conscious, you should be fighting the South and freeing the slaves. You don't build conscious minds just to make them work for free.

After dinner, Navon sent Olah his research: if building conscious machines inevitably creates a slave class, building them must be outlawed.

Olah’s quiet line to the Times:
"We don’t know if AI models are conscious. I don’t know. I’m genuinely uncertain."

quoted_text:
What happens when you can trade the parts of an asset?
We’re still thinking too narrowly about tokenization.

We talk about putting stocks, property, commodities and other assets onchain. There are good reasons to do that. But the part that is missing is what people could build around those assets once they’re there.

Owning something usually means accepting a package of things you may not want equally.

Someone buys a property for the rent. Someone else buys it because they think the neighborhood will become more valuable. A third person likes the property but needs predictable income for the next year.

They can agree that the asset is worth owning while wanting very different things from it.That is the kind of market Sazare wants to explore.

The starting point is splitting a token into FLOOR and UPSIDE. The idea is to give people separate ways to participate in the floor-related economics and coupon income, or in the more speculative part of the asset’s value.

A holder could keep one side and sell the other. A new buyer could choose the exposure they actually came for.

There is an important distinction in the current design: matching FLOOR and UPSIDE can be recombined into the underlying token, but the market decides how much each piece is worth. FLOOR on its own is not a guaranteed redemption at the underlying floor.

Even with that distinction, there is a lot worth building. And many ways the idea can be improved and iterated upon. 

You might believe a market will stay active for years without having a strong opinion about where its token trades next week. You might want the upside and have little interest in collecting coupons. Or you might already own the asset and want to recover some capital while keeping part of your exposure.

Today, those views are often pushed into the same buy-or-sell decision. Separate instruments give people more room to express them.The fixed-term desk is where I think this becomes especially useful.

Variable income is attractive until you need to plan around it.

Suppose you hold a coupon-bearing position and would rather know what you will receive over the next ninety days. A desk could let you exchange that period’s variable coupons for a payment agreed in advance.

Someone else takes the other side because they think the income will be worth more than they are paying.
You get a defined payment. They get the uncertain receipts. Neither person needs to be wrong for the trade to make sense.

A treasury might value the certainty because it has expenses to meet. A trader might expect a busy quarter. A longer-term holder might give up a few months of income without wanting to sell their entire position.

Over time, you could have prices for thirty days, ninety days, six months or a year of exposure. Those prices would tell us something different from a spot chart: what people are willing to pay for income over time.
And I don’t think that idea should stop at crypto-native tokens.

Take a tokenized interest in a building. If the token carries enforceable rights to rental income, there could eventually be markets for that income over a particular period, alongside exposure to the property’s longer-term value. An owner might sell a year of eligible distributions to fund a renovation. A buyer might prefer that defined period to owning a property interest indefinitely.

With music, the underlying right could be royalties from a catalog. An artist might want money today to fund a tour or another recording. Someone else might be willing to buy a defined share of future receipts. The terms would determine exactly what changes hands and what the artist keeps.

For compute, the asset might be a claim on future GPU hours or revenue from supplying capacity. One participant could want predictable receipts to cover equipment costs. Another could take a view on demand over the next few months.

The same questions could arise around energy production, equipment leases, receivables, licensing rights or assets that do not have a widely used token standard yet.

Who wants to own the asset? Who wants its income? Who wants a particular period of exposure? Who is willing to pay for certainty, and who is willing to accept the uncertainty?

Those are useful questions wherever something valuable can be tokenized.

That does not mean every token should be forced into the same structure. A claim on electricity, a stock and a music royalty have different rights and different ways of settling. Some assets produce income directly. Others might support coupons funded by trading activity. Those sources should stay clearly distinguished.

Tokenization also cannot fix a right that is unenforceable, create backing that does not exist, or promise a payment nobody has funded.
What Sazare wants is a foundation that can accommodate those differences as the assets and integrations develop.

There is plenty of work between that ambition and a useful market. People need understandable contracts, reliable accounting, sensible collateral rules and enough liquidity to leave a position. A fixed-term payment needs defined obligations and funding behind it. Splitting an asset does not remove its risks.

But this direction is worth pursuing.

A person should be able to say, “I want the income for the next six months,” or “I want to keep the upside but sell some of the income,” and find a market that understands that request.

As more things become tokenized, the number of possible choices grows with them.
